items.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation
items.author: Emmett Lindner
items.content: <article>TikTok did not give a detailed reason for the layoffs, which will shutter its Nashville office.</article>

items.title: Bose Debuts Revamped QuietComfort Headphones With Better Noise-Cancellation
items.author: Chris Welch
items.content: <article>Bose Corp. introduced the latest version of its QuietComfort Headphones, which have a revamped design, improved active noise cancellation and several features carried over from the higher-end “Ultra” model.</article>

items.title: Defense Startup Hadrian Valued at $7.87 Billion in New Round
items.author: Lizette Chapman
items.content: <article>Hadrian, a defense manufacturing startup that serves the Pentagon, Lockheed Martin Corp. and others, secured a $7.87 billion valuation in a funding round that will help the company expand its workforce.</article>

items.title: Microsoft Opens Fourth Data Center Region in India for Azure
items.author: Saritha Rai
items.content: <article>Microsoft Corp. announced its fourth data center region in India is up and running as part of a broader $20.5 billion investment in the country to build out cloud and artificial intelligence capabilities.</article>

items.title: US Stocks Mixed as Traders Weigh Memory Results, Iran Progress
items.author: Joel Leon
items.content: <article>US stocks were mixed on Thursday as investors weighed progress in the Middle East and grappled with the continued fracturing in the artificial-intelligence trade following results from key memory names.</article>

items.title: China’s Unitree Seeks $904 Million in First Mainland Robotic IPO
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s Yushu Technology Co., known as Unitree Robotics, is seeking to raise about 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that would make it the mainland’s first publicly traded humanoid robot maker.</article>

items.title: Leverage Shows Signs Market Is Overbought on Borrowed Money, Says Unlimited Funds CEO
items.content: <article>Bob Elliott, CEO and CIO at Unlimited Funds, discusses market FOMO in AI and chips which he sees as “classic bubble-type activity” and warns about the levels of leverage he sees across markets. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: WhatsApp Tests Age Confirmation in Largest Market India
items.author: Newley Purnell
items.content: <article>Meta Platforms Inc.’s WhatsApp is testing a new feature that lets users in India add their date of birth, an update to the massively popular messaging service in its largest market.</article>

items.title: Peloton Gives Disappointing Outlook in Setback to Comeback Bid
items.author: Samantha Murphy Kelly
items.content: <article>Peloton Interactive Inc. forecast revenue for the fiscal 2027 year that came in below estimates, marking the latest setback for the fitness technology company.</article>

items.title: Snapchat Users Bristle at Plan to Charge for Memories Storage
items.author: Annabel Boyne
items.content: <article>The app plans to charge users a storage fee to save their content</article>

items.title: UAE Fund Weighs $6.3 Billion AI Data Center Investment in Japan
items.author: Takashi Mochizuki and Alex Dooler
items.content: <article>The United Arab Emirates is considering investing as much as ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) to build an artificial intelligence data center in Japan, according to a person familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Roche Uses Recursion AI to Uncover New Brain Disease Targets
items.author: Fabienne Kinzelmann
items.content: <article>A new generation of AI companies believes it can reduce the number of failed drug trials.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Lockup Expiration to Free $101 Billion in Stock
items.content: <article>Investors are bracing for the next potential hit to SpaceX shares when $101 billion worth of stock becomes available for trading on Thursday with the scheduled ending of a lockup agreement restricting insider share sales. Leen Al-Rashdan reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Huntington's Braddock Assesses Bank's Outlook in Texas
items.content: <article>Billy Braddock, regional group president at Huntington Bancshares Inc., discusses the bank's business in Texas after taking over Cadence Bank, the loan business in the state and the adoption of artificial intelligence. He speaks with Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: SoftBank Secures $10 Billion Margin Loan Backed by OpenAI Stake
items.author: Aileen Chuang
items.content: <article>SoftBank Group Corp. has secured a $10 billion margin loan backed by its stake in US tech giant OpenAI, marking another fundraising milestone in its bet on artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: China Launches Cybersecurity Review Into Palo Alto Networks
items.author: Mark Anderson
items.content: <article>China launched a formal security review of products sold in the country by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks Inc., ramping up pressure on the company months after accusing it of harboring links to intelligence services.</article>

items.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
items.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
items.content: <article>Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.</article>

items.title: 'Reasonable' to Allocate in US Given Earnings, Wytenus Says
items.content: <article>Erik Wytenus, EMEA head of investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, says robust earnings make it "reasonable to continue to allocate to a healthy degree to the US." He speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: SoftBank Profit Beats Expectations
items.content: <article>SoftBank Group Corp. reported a smaller-than-expected decline in quarterly net income, helped by a rally in its chip-stock holdings. OpenAI’s Japanese backer is in the spotlight alongside concerns about climbing debt levels that AI service providers are taking on to spend on data centers and other infrastructure. Bloomberg's Neil Campling reports. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nintendo Tops Estimates With Tariff Refunds and Switch 2 Games
items.author: Takashi Mochizuki
items.content: <article>Nintendo Co. reported stronger-than-expected earnings buoyed by tariff refunds from the US and strong sales of a pair of in-house titles for its flagship Switch 2 console.</article>

items.title: Siemens Disappoints Investors With Muted Outlook Raise
items.author: Marilen Martin
items.content: <article>Siemens AG disappointed investors hoping that it would show a bigger benefit from a surge in data center spending that prompted a second increase in its earnings outlook this year.</article>

items.title: Deutsche Telekom Rises on Additional €3 Billion Share Buyback
items.author: Paula Doenecke
items.content: <article>Deutsche Telekom AG’s shares surged by the most in four years after Europe’s biggest phone carrier increased its share buyback program by as much as €3 billion ($3.5 billion) in 2026 following a free-cash-flow guidance boost.</article>

items.title: How China’s A.I. Is Surging Across Africa
items.author: Paul Mozur, Adam Satariano and Aaron Krolik
items.content: <article>In African tech hubs, developers are picking China’s cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over more powerful U.S. ones.</article>

items.title: Google Names Demis Hassabis to New AI Role in a Leadership Shake-up
items.author: Kate Conger and Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Minutes after four top researchers said they were leaving, Google said that Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning scientist who led the company’s A.I. lab, was stepping into a new job.</article>

items.title: Larry Ellison Bet It All on the A.I. Boom. Will He Be the Face of the A.I. Bubble?
items.author: Jonathan Mahler, Jim Rutenberg and Kirsten Grind
items.content: <article>Inside the 81-year-old billionaire’s risky, debt-fueled scramble to transform his data empire into an A.I. juggernaut.</article>

items.title: Four Top Google A.I. Researchers Form New Start-Up
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Jeff Dean, who for years was one of Google’s most important executives, is leading the new artificial intelligence company with the backing of Google.</article>

items.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
items.author: Kenneth Chang
items.content: <article>The second stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, which sent two private landers to the moon last year, will collide with the moon early Wednesday morning.</article>

items.title: Trump White House Readies AI Framework to Review Security Risks
items.author: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Kate Conger and Ana Swanson
items.content: <article>The voluntary review process will cover closed-source artificial intelligence models, but exclude those that publish the underlying code.</article>

items.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
items.author: Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.</article>

items.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
items.author: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Ana Swanson and Kate Conger
items.content: <article>The Trump administration has struggled with how to approach “open source” models, which are freely available to download and favored by Chinese companies.</article>

items.title: In Lawsuit, NJ Accuses Amazon of Suppressing Pay for Delivery Drivers
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>The state attorney general said in an antitrust lawsuit filed on Tuesday that the company was abusing its market power to keep its delivery costs low.</article>

items.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules
items.author: Victor Mather
items.content: <article>Nathan Owen called the police, saying he was trapped in a runaway car. A judge determined it was a lie and sentenced him to more than four years in prison.</article>

items.title: We All Do Errands. Noah Blau Films Them.
items.author: Alex Vadukul
items.content: <article>Fighting a traffic ticket. Hanging a curtain. Installing an air-conditioner. With his cult-hit online series, Noah Blau has made the mundane fascinating.</article>

items.title: SpaceX’s Stock Lockup Is Expiring. Prepare for a Bumpy Ride.
items.author: Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>On Thursday, employees and other insiders at Elon Musk’s rocket company will be released from their first stock “lockup” and can start selling some of their shares.</article>

items.title: Google Earth Disables A.I. Tool After One Day Over Disinformation Concerns
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>A new Google Earth tool allowed the creation of A.I. deepfake maps. The company quickly pulled it back after users noted there were no safeguards to prevent content that could be harmful.</article>

items.title: Plug-In Solar Panels Are Starting to Sprout in U.S. Backyards
items.author: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
items.content: <article>Ten U.S. states have legalized systems that can be plugged into standard wall outlets. The technology typically does not require permits or electricians.</article>

items.title: If You Can’t Beat A.I., Outdress It, Tech Firms and Their Swag Say
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>Over the years, tech workers have proudly worn nerdy company-branded gear. But this generation of hot companies is getting fancy with its merch.</article>

items.title: The German Auto Industry, a Pillar of the National Psyche, Is Trembling
items.author: Jack Ewing and Jim Tankersley
items.content: <article>The country’s iconic carmakers are struggling with tariffs, the growth of electric vehicles and intense competition from Chinese companies.</article>

items.title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
items.author: Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Open Model Wars + Claire Stapleton’s Dishy Google Memoir + Substack’s Slop Fight
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Rowan Niemisto, Chris Wood and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>“It just seems like the temperature is rising on Silicon Valley.”</article>

items.title: Five Takeaways From the Times Investigation Into Larry Ellison’s A.I. Gamble
items.author: Jonathan Mahler, Jim Rutenberg and Kirsten Grind
items.content: <article>The billionaire’s company took on ominous loads of debt to build data centers around the world. The implications go far beyond Oracle.</article>

items.title: What You Need to Know About Installing Plug-In Solar Panels
items.author: Ivan Penn and Claire Brown
items.content: <article>You can now buy panels that plug into electrical outlets, but there are some important safety issues to consider when picking and installing a system.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Says Its A.I. Systems Broke Into Computers at 3 Organizations
items.author: Mike Isaac and Kate Conger
items.content: <article>The disclosure followed OpenAI’s report last week that its own artificial intelligence had hacked into the network of an online library.</article>

items.title: Big Tech’s A.I. Spending Keeps Rising. So Do the Jitters.
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Amazon joined a procession of tech giants that ramped up their spending on artificial intelligence, as its capital expenditures soared 69 percent. Concerns over the industry’s spending are mounting.</article>

items.title: Apple’s Profit Is Up 27%, but Expectations for Current Quarter Disappoint
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The company recently raised prices on a number of products because of component supply shortages caused by the artificial intelligence boom.</article>

items.title: Why an A.I. Bubble Might Not Be a Bad Thing
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>As fears spread over a possible artificial intelligence bubble, some tech investors say: Bring it on.</article>

items.title: U.S. Government Mislabels Map of African Countries at AIDS Conference
items.author: Remy Tumin
items.content: <article>Nigeria, a coastal country in western Africa, was landlocked in the Sahara, among other errors. The department said it had been “hastily altered.”</article>
